## Abstract

SLR Suite is an RStudio and Quarto workflow that links systematic-review protocols, executable analysis stages, validation evidence, and reporting. This software revision replaces a stateful launcher with isolated orchestration functions, adds explicit dependency and project metadata, introduces automated structural tests, and records reproducibility evidence in machine-readable artifacts. The bundled example supports verification of the workflow mechanics; it is not presented as evidence for substantive literature-review conclusions.

## Introduction

Systematic literature reviews require traceable decisions from search design through reporting. Earlier versions of SLR Suite combined scripts and documentation but did not provide a stable RStudio project contract, an explicit validation protocol, or a complete manuscript that described the executable architecture. This revision treats software, documentation, experimentation, and the paper as one research object.

## Software architecture

The system has six layers: orchestration (`R/`), numbered analysis stages (`scripts/`), protocol configuration (`config/`), evidence (`data/`), validation (`tests/` and `experiments/`), and reporting (`docs/`). Pipeline stages execute in isolated environments and append outcome records to a CSV log. Dependencies are declared before execution; the launcher does not mutate the user's global workspace or install packages at runtime.

## Methods

The validation experiment checks eight repository invariants: RStudio metadata, dependency metadata, search and screening protocols, an example input, at least nine ordered analysis stages, automated tests, and the manuscript. The experiment records the runtime platform, R version, timestamp, and individual pass/fail outcomes. GitHub Actions runs the same validation and test entry points on each proposed change.

## Results

The revised repository supplies an RStudio project, reusable orchestration functions, regression tests, a deterministic validation command, CI automation, user documentation, architecture documentation, and this manuscript. Quantitative bibliometric results are intentionally not claimed here until a frozen corpus, preregistered parameter set, and independently checked outputs are available.

## Limitations

Structural validation establishes that declared components are present and executable; it does not establish search completeness, screening reliability, coding validity, or correctness of domain interpretations. The included raw export is an example dataset and should not be generalized beyond workflow testing.

## Reproducibility and availability

Open `slr-suite.Rproj`, install dependencies from `DESCRIPTION`, run `Rscript tests/testthat.R`, and then run `Rscript master_launcher.R validate`. Generated validation evidence is written under `artifacts/validation/`. Source code and version history are available from the project repository.

## Conclusion

The revision turns SLR Suite from a collection of scripts into a documented and testable research workflow. Its principal contribution is the explicit alignment of protocol, code execution, validation evidence, and manuscript claims.
